findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral transition (e.g., "Separately") or present the two facts as independent items.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this parallels the prior sentence, but updating a log yearly and tracking a catalog monthly are different cadences, so the connective misrepresents the relationship.

findings.evidence: "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month" / "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year" / "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year"
findings.fix: State once, in one place, who owns the catalog and how often it's updated, and delete the conflicting duplicate statements.
findings.location: Program Overview vs. Special Cases vs. Questions and Updates
findings.violation: Three different sections attribute equipment-catalog maintenance to three different teams on two different schedules (monthly vs. annually), which is contradictory.

findings.evidence: "one claim per employee per benefit year" vs. "at the start of the fiscal year"
findings.fix: Define both terms explicitly, or standardize on a single term throughout the document.
findings.violation: The document uses both "benefit year" and "fiscal year" without clarifying whether they refer to the same period, leaving eligibility timing ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Replace "stipend clock" with the specific period it refers to.
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined - it's unclear whether it refers to the 90-day service requirement or the benefit-year claim window.

findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year." vs. "the policy applies to one device per category per employee"
findings.fix: Clarify whether the per-benefit-year limit is a single overall claim or one per category.
findings.location: Eligibility section vs. Restrictions and Exceptions section
findings.violation: It's unclear whether an employee can make only one claim total per year or one claim per equipment category, which is a contradiction in claim limits.

findings.evidence: "Also, the portal saves a draft automatically every few minutes. Employees can return to finish later without losing progress."
findings.fix: Remove this detail or move it to portal help documentation rather than the policy steps.
findings.violation: This sentence adds no policy-relevant information and interrupts the step-by-step description of the application process with an unrelated portal feature.

findings.evidence: "an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives"
findings.fix: Specify what "missing item" refers to (e.g., the missing receipt or documentation).
findings.violation: "The missing item" is never identified, making the rule impossible to apply consistently.

findings.evidence: "within two business days" vs. "an automatic reminder after three days"

findings.violation: The timeline mixes "business days" and plain "days" without clarifying whether the reminder period is calendar or business days.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: List which request types require additional documentation, or remove the qualifier.
findings.violation: "Most requests" implies exceptions requiring more documentation, but none are specified anywhere in the document.

findings.violation: This shifts to second-/first-person voice ("You", "we"), inconsistent with the third-person voice used everywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Remove "Similarly" or replace with a neutral transition.
findings.violation: "Similarly" falsely implies this rule parallels the prior sentence about annual photo checks, when the two are unrelated topics.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... You submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Convert to third person to match the rest of the document.
findings.violation: This section again shifts to second-person voice, inconsistent with the third-person voice used elsewhere.

findings.evidence: heading "Terminology Notes" followed by "Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Either add actual definitions of key terms (e.g., "stipend item," "stipend request") or rename/remove the section.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt." vs. "Employees start a stipend request in the benefits portal... reviews the confirmation summary before submitting"

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out." vs. "The manager reviews the request within two business days."
